Priam. The aged king of Troy who ruled throughout the entire ten-year war, he witnessed the destruction of his kingdom while grieving the loss of his many sons. He was married to Hecuba, enduring her prophecies of doom and the terrible visions that foreshadowed Troy's fate. Priam fathered numerous children, including the mighty Hector, the ill-fated Paris, and the prophetic Cassandra, whose lives would all shape the course of the war. He made the fateful decision to allow Paris to abduct Helen, which directly triggered the Greek invasion. As the war raged year after year, Priam watched helplessly as his sons fell one by one in battle. The most devastating blow came when he watched his greatest son, Hector, die at the hands of Achilles. After Hector's death, Priam was forced to humble himself, going before Achilles himself to ransom his son's body so that it could receive proper burial rites. Throughout these horrors, he maintained his role as king and protector of his people, retaining dignity even as the city's inevitable downfall approached. When Troy finally fell, Priam was killed by Achilles' son Neoptolemus at the altar of the gods, bringing his reign and his life to a tragic end.
